=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:360-393 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The collector's local redaction (`_LOG_TAIL_SECRET_PATTERNS` / `_redact_log_text`) copies only the seven simple `workflow_failure_heal._SECRET_PATTERNS` regexes and leaves out the encoded-credential pass in `heal.redact_secrets` (`re.sub(r"[A-Za-z0-9+/_-]{24,}={0,2}", _redact_encoded_credential, text)`, scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3453-3455), so base64 `x-access-token:` / `user:token` credentials reach `failed[i].log_tail` unmasked.
  WHY: No generic redaction runs again downstream (check_failure_triage.sh cats PR_CHECK_RUNS_CONTEXT_FILE straight into the prompt; the reviewer/editor prompts also consume it), the triage path masks the same log with the full `heal.redact_secrets` (check_triage_resolution.py:873-874), and the README.md:162 and agents.d/8799-triage-log-anchor.md:2 wording ("Credential shapes are masked on the whole scan") claims more than the code does. Reviewers disagree on severity: gemini, minimax and luna rate it MAJOR; sonnet and glm rate it NIT because it is not a regression (the collector had no redaction before this PR). The highest rating (MAJOR, mapped to high) is used here.
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:365-378 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The unbounded scheme quantifier in `_LOG_TAIL_SECRET_PATTERNS[0]` (`r"([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://)[^/@\s]+@"`) backtracks quadratically on long alphanumeric runs that contain no `://`, and it now runs over every scan of up to LOG_SCAN_BYTES (262,144 bytes).
  WHY: Output stays correct, but each failed check-run whose log holds a long hex/base64 line (such as the incident's 65,565-byte initcode hex line) costs seconds of CPU in the collector; this cost is new to the collector. All reviewers rate it NIT.
- scripts/check_triage_resolution.py:785-806 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_step_error_window` counts the up-to-5 trailing lines inside the `MAX_EXCERPT_LINES` budget (`before = lines[max(0, index + 1 + after - MAX_EXCERPT_LINES):index]`), so pre-error context shrinks below the spec's "MAX_EXCERPT_LINES lines ending at it, plus up to 5 after".
  WHY: When the log has enough preceding lines, the excerpt loses about 5 lines immediately above the error; glm notes the cause line itself can fall in that band. Reviewers state the shortfall differently (gemini: 114 lines / 6 lost; minimax: starts at index - 114; luna: 115 lines; glm: index - 114). All rate it NIT. Sonnet reported CORRECTNESS NONE.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  expected_change_site: tests/test_collect_pr_check_runs_context.py
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The requested new test module is absent from the PR's changed files. The collector tests (test_window_ends_at_the_step_error_not_the_teardown_dump, test_log_without_step_error_keeps_the_old_tail, test_credentials_are_redacted_before_the_line_cut, and others) live in tests/test_collect_pr_check_runs_pending_identity.py:404-641 instead. The `tests/**` grant covers that placement. An earlier editor round recorded an explicit ignore (the existing file is already wired into CI; a new module would need ci.yml wiring) plus a CONSOLIDATOR_OVERRIDDEN entry. Sonnet deliberately did not raise this gap, citing .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 3080/743 and the "§27: no workflow file changes" constraint.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:_LOG_TAIL_SECRET_PATTERNS (lines 364-372) and _redact_log_text (lines 375-378), called from _select_log_tail_window at line 393 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The local redaction copy has only the seven credential-shape regexes from workflow_failure_heal._SECRET_PATTERNS (scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py lines 3430-3439). It leaves out the encoded-credential pass at lines 3453-3455, so base64 "x-access-token:<token>" or "user:<36+ char secret>" pairs not preceded by "Basic " pass through unchanged.
  WHY: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh lines 1724-1729 run the collector, and line 1880 cats PR_CHECK_RUNS_CONTEXT_FILE into the prompt. The later redaction (lines 2109-2113) replaces only the literal token value. Not a regression, but README/agents.d wording overpromises.
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:line 365, re.compile(r"([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://)[^/@\s]+@"), applied by _redact_log_text to the whole decoded scan at line 393 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The unbounded scheme quantifier backtracks quadratically on long alphanumeric runs with no "://" across the up-to-262,144-byte scan.
  WHY: Seconds of CPU for a 65 KB run (more near 256 KB). The cost is new to the collector.
- Other categories reported NONE, including TASK COMPLETENESS. Sonnet explicitly declined to raise the missing tests/test_collect_pr_check_runs_context.py, citing ci.yml explicit lists (line 3080, line 743) and the no-workflow-changes constraint. It also noted the copilot-pull-request-reviewer failure (HTTP 422, custom_instructions_too_large) is external, and that collection_status: timeout with 11 incomplete check-runs means CI is unconfirmed.
- HARDENING (2 related items): (1) _redact_log_text (lines 375-378): add a local copy of the encoded-credential pass (~10 lines), or narrow the README/agents.d wording (2 lines). (2) line 365: bound the scheme to r"([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]{0,31}://)[^/@\s]+@" with a comment (2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:_LOG_TAIL_SECRET_PATTERNS (lines 364-374) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_redact_log_text` implements only a subset of simple patterns and omits the second-pass base64-encoded credential scan that `heal.redact_secrets` performs.
  WHY: Base64-encoded credentials pass through unmasked into `failed[i].log_tail` and the PR review context, violating the full-text redaction requirement.
- scripts/check_triage_resolution.py:_step_error_window (lines 786-790) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The window counts the 5 trailing lines inside the `MAX_EXCERPT_LINES` (120) budget.
  WHY: Only 114 lines of preceding context are kept, losing 6 lines of diagnostic data compared with the spec.
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:_LOG_TAIL_SECRET_PATTERNS[0] (line 366) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The unbounded scheme quantifier in `r"([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://)[^/@\s]+@"` can cause catastrophic backtracking.
  WHY: It runs on every scan of up to 256 KB; long lines such as the 65 KB initcode hex cause significant CPU use and delay triage.
- HARDENING: line 366: bound the scheme to `r"([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]{0,31}://)[^/@\s]+@"` (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:lines 360-378 (the new `_LOG_TAIL_SECRET_PATTERNS` and `_redact_log_text` added by LAST RUN DIFF); also line 393 where `_redact_log_text` is wired into `_select_log_tail_window` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The collector redaction is a partial copy of `workflow_failure_heal.redact_secrets` and omits the encoded-credential scan at `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3455`, while triage calls the full `heal.redact_secrets` (line 874 of check_triage_resolution.py).
  WHY: A base64 x-access-token in a job log (e.g. `git config --get-regexp http.extraheader` output) ends up in `failed[i].log_tail` and from there in the reviewer/editor prompts (`scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`, `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`) and triage comments. The README overstates the masking.
- scripts/check_triage_resolution.py:lines 785-806, specifically the `before = lines[max(0, index + 1 + after - MAX_EXCERPT_LINES):index]` slice at line 789 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `MAX_EXCERPT_LINES` is treated as a total budget that includes the trailing lines, so `before` starts at `index - 114`.
  WHY: 5 lines of pre-error context are trimmed against the spec; the error line survives, so this is a context deviation, not a correctness break.
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:line 365 — `re.compile(r"([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://)[^/@\s]+@")` is now run by `_redact_log_text` on every scan up to `LOG_SCAN_BYTES` (262144 bytes) at line 393 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The unbounded `*` scheme quantifier and the `[^/@\s]+` body backtrack on long alphanumeric runs with no `://` (ReDoS shape).
  WHY: Seconds of CPU per long hex/base64 line, multiplied across check-runs. The collector previously did no redaction, so the cost is new.

  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
